findings.title: raw_html posts are served with no sanitization (stored XSS)
findings.body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == raw_html`. For imported content this means RSS item bodies (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)`) and `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls` output (a Nokogiri round-trip that does not sanitize) are stored as `cooked`. They are then rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in the regular topic view. `<script>`, `onerror=` handlers and `javascript:` links in a feed or page therefore execute on the forum origin. The `import_remote` path restricts tags, but the RSS path does not. Run the HTML through a whitelist sanitizer (e.g. `Sanitize`) at import or in `cook`.

findings.title: Embed URL interpolated into HTML unescaped; URL check uses `^` instead of `\A`
findings.body: The footer is built as `"#{url}"` with no escaping, and that string goes into a post that is never sanitized (raw_html). The only guard is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` on line 11. `^` matches at any line start, so a value like `"junk\nhttp://x"` passes. A `'` in a feed-supplied link (for example `http://a/' onmouseover='...`) breaks out of the attribute. Anchor the check with `\A`, parse the URL, and escape it with `ERB::Util.h` or `CGI.escapeHTML`.

findings.title: import mutates the caller's contents string in place
findings.body: `contents << "...footer..."` appends to the string passed in. This breaks on frozen strings and has surprising side effects for callers that reuse the string, such as the spec's `let(:contents)` or the Disqus importer. Use `contents = contents + footer` or build a new local string.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs and ignores other relative paths
findings.body: The `start_with?('/')` check also matches protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png`. `sub(/^\/+/, '')` then strips every leading slash and yields `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example.com/a.png`, a broken link or image. The same bug is on line 71 for `src`. Relative paths without a leading slash (`images/x.png`, `../x`) are not resolved at all, even though the method is documented as converting relative URLs to absolute. Use `URI.join(url, href)` for non-absolute values and skip anything that already has a scheme or a `//` prefix.

findings.title: embed.post can be nil (soft-deleted post), crashing the update path
findings.body: `post = embed.post` goes through Post's trashable default scope. If the imported post or topic was deleted, the association returns nil. When the content hash changes, `PostRevisor.new(nil).revise!` then raises NoMethodError on `nil.raw`. In `PollFeed` this aborts the whole `rss.items.each` loop, so one deleted topic blocks all later imports every hour. Guard against a nil post, and either skip it or recreate the topic.

findings.title: Disqus importer silently loses --category option and original topic created_at
findings.body: The `-c/--category` option and its lookup are removed, and `PostCreator` is replaced by `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. All imported topics now land in the default category, and `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` is dropped, so topics get today's date instead of the Disqus thread date. The importer now also does a live HTTP fetch of every thread link via `open(url).read`, with no error handling. A single 404 or timeout raises and aborts the whole import. None of this is mentioned in the PR.

findings.title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds destructive `force: true`
findings.body: This PR rewrites an already-existing migration (`create_top_topics`) to use `force: true`, which drops and recreates `top_topics` if the migration is ever re-run. That is unrelated to embedding and destructive. `create_topic_embeds` also uses `force: true` (line 3) and would drop an existing `topic_embeds` table and its data. Editing historical migrations, and the whitespace-only change to `migrate_word_counts`, should be left out of this PR.

findings.title: New gems added without updating the Rails 3 lockfile
findings.body: `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` are added to the shared Gemfile, but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated. The repo is dual-booted, and `Gemfile.lock` (RAILS3=1 mode) is not touched. Bundler in that mode will have to re-resolve, or fail with a frozen or deployment lockfile, and CI for the Rails 3 boot is likely to break.

findings.title: embed.css / embed.js not added to the asset precompile list
findings.body: The layout calls `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, and `embed.js` is meant to be loaded by third-party sites. Neither asset is added to `config.assets.precompile` (no change to `config/application.rb` in this PR). With precompiled assets in production the stylesheet raises or 404s, so the embed iframe renders unstyled or errors. `embed.js` will not be served either.

findings.title: Referer interpolated into an inline JS string with HTML escaping only
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` places a request header inside a JavaScript string using HTML escaping, which is the wrong context. A backslash is not escaped, so a referer ending in `\` breaks the string and the script. Escaped entities such as `'` are not decoded inside `<script>`, so the value is mangled. It should be emitted with `.to_json` or `j()`. It is also better to use the origin derived from the validated `embeddable_host` than the raw header.

findings.title: Origin check is a substring test
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` only checks that the message origin is a substring of the configured URL. A different-origin sender can match, for example `https://example.com` against `https://example.com:8080/`. Compare against the exact origin of `discourseUrl` and also check `e.source === iframe.contentWindow`.

findings.title: Nil item content or one bad item aborts the whole feed poll
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no `content` (common for RSS items that only have `description`). There is no per-item rescue, so one bad entry stops processing of all remaining items on every hourly run. The same loop also reaches the nil-post crash in `TopicEmbed.import`. Handle nil content (fall back to `description`/`summary`) and rescue per item so one failure doesn't block the rest.

findings.title: Each unknown embed URL can trigger a full synchronous feed poll
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an unknown embed URL is requested. The throttle key is per URL, so requests for many different URLs each fetch and parse the entire feed and import every item in a Sidekiq worker, with no timeout. Since the `embed/best` endpoint enqueues this job for any unseen URL, it is an easy amplification path. Throttle at the feed level (e.g. one key for the feed URL) rather than per embed URL.

findings.title: Embeddability gate relies solely on the Referer header
findings.body: Access is allowed only if `request.referer`'s host equals `embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled and trivially spoofed by non-browser clients, and is dropped for legitimate embeds when the embedding page sets a strict Referrer-Policy. Those embeds get an InvalidAccess error. Also, `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value, and framing is unrestricted once the Referer check passes. Consider CSP `frame-ancestors` for the configured host.

findings.title: Malformed `<%- end if %>` closes the conditional with a modifier
findings.body: `end if` turns the following generated statement into an `if` modifier condition on the whole if/else block. It only works by accident because the next generated expression is a truthy string append. It reads as a typo and is fragile against template changes. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: "is 404 without an embed_url" passes for the wrong reason
findings.body: With no stubs, `embeddable_host` is blank, so the request fails in `ensure_embeddable` before `params.require(:embed_url)` is ever reached, and the failure is an InvalidAccess response, not a 404. The missing-parameter path is never exercised. There is also no test for a referer whose host differs from `embeddable_host`. The new `PollFeed#poll_feed`, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` and the update branch of `import` also have no meaningful coverage.
